chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, together from Ahmad ibn Is'haq, from Sa'dan, from more than one person — they traced it back (marfu') to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the people of Kufa — had they performed tahnik upon their newborn children with the water of the Euphrates, they would have been our Shia.

key_terms.الْفُرَاتِ: The Euphrates (Al-Furat) — the great river near Kufa, considered sacred in Shia tradition, near whose banks Imam Husayn was martyred at Karbala
key_terms.حَنَّكُوا: Tahnik — the Sunnah of rubbing the palate of a newborn with a softened date or other blessed substance, performed to bless the child at birth
key_terms.رَفَعُوهُ: Marfu' — a technical hadith term meaning the chain was 'raised' or attributed upward to a higher authority (here, to Imam Ali)
key_terms.شِيعَةً: Shia — followers, partisans, here referring to sincere and committed followers of the Imams (Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the virtue of the water of the Euphrates according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) reflects on the spiritual potential of the people of Kufa, stating that if they had performed the ritual of tahnik (rubbing the palate of a newborn with a blessed substance) using the sacred water of the Euphrates River, they would have become true Shia. This statement underscores the spiritual virtue ascribed to the water of the Euphrates in Shia tradition and the ritual significance of tahnik in nurturing children with religious blessing. The people of Kufa, though historically significant as a Shia center, fell short of full loyalty to the Imam, and this hadith speaks to the formative power of blessed rituals.
word_analysis: they performed tahnik (welcomed with rubbed substance)
